messages:
alex: Heads-up: eu-west1 dedicated GPU pool at ~98% allocation, request queue spiking, some jobs pending >60s. Alerting from prometheus :warning:
ops-bot: [alert] eu-west1.dedicated.gpu_pool util=98% queue=421 p95=1.2s
sophie: Is this a slow ramp or sudden burst? any deploys/rollouts right before this?
mike: Sudden. We pushed a tiny networkpolicy tweak at 02:12 that restricts pod-to-pod probe traffic for kube-system. I see a spike in NotReady flaps right after that.
tanvi: Autoscaler logic skipped a scale-up because many nodes got the `maintenance=true` taint from last night's drain job. NP change + taint meant new pods couldn't land on nodes that were otherwise healthy.
jamie: Kicking off emergency mitigation: routing more requests to hosted capacity (prefer low-priority traffic) and warming model caches. Will do a conservative weight bump first.
alex: How big a weight bump? and any quick cmd to run?
jamie: +30% hosted weight for low-priority traffic to start. Command I'm running from control-plane: ```rctl route update --region eu-west1 --add-hosted-weight 30 --filter priority<=low```
mike: Rolling back the networkpolicy patch now — probe traffic was being dropped: diff shows `deny from kube-system:probes -> drop`. Rolling to previous ruleset.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for np/kube-prober at 03:18 UTC (eu-west1), status: in_progress
sophie: Cost heads-up: hosted absorb will increase spend. Can we gate hosted fallback to small-models or token-capped requests while dedicated recovers?
tanvi: Good call — adding model-size filter and a token cap: route requests <=2k tokens to hosted. Also decreasing autoscaler scale-up cooldown from 5m -> 60s so we can recover capacity faster once nodes are ready.
alex: Any cache/cold-start issues when we move traffic to hosted variants?
jamie: We'll prefer the `slim` model-variant on hosted to reduce memory and token cost; pre-warming top prefixes for top 10 orgs now.
mike: Nodes are coming back after rollback, starting to remove maintenance taints on recovered workers. ETA for dedicated capacity ~6 minutes if no surprises.
oncall-night: Observability: queue length dropped ~40% since weight bump. Error rates stable, a few 503s during transition but trending down. Keeping monitoring on high.
sophie: Post-incident tasks: 1) revoke that NP change and add stricter review for probe-affecting rules, 2) autoscaler: respect taint->scale decision to allow emergency scheduling, 3) add a runbook entry for hosted-weight emergency shifts and cost caps. @mike @tanvi please own 1 & 2.
alex: I'll leave hosted relief in place for 20m then ramp back to normal if metrics look good. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident note: temporary hosted fallback active, rollback of np in progress. Will update when dedicated pool stable.
